analysis.title: China in 2027: Finding growth amid managed stability
key_insights: UBS CIO expects China GDP growth in the mid-4% range in 2027 after 4.6% in 2026, with slower exports, stabilized consumption and better investment.

Exports rose around 20% y/y in 2026, with AI-related products about half of export growth. UBS expects export growth to slow to the high single digits in 2027 as AI capex growth moderates and the comparison base rises.

The 'Six Networks' initiative envisages CNY 25tr of government-led investment during the 15th Five-Year Plan, covering power grids, computing infrastructure, communications and logistics. UBS expects investment to improve after its sharp contraction in 2026.

Policy is expected to stay modestly expansionary with targeted support for technology localization, strategic infrastructure, consumer subsidies and social welfare, not broad stimulus. Property is unlikely to get large-scale support and should remain a drag.
Monetary policy should stay accommodative through RRR cuts, credit facilities and liquidity injections. Elevated global bond yields limit room for large policy-rate cuts.
UBS stays Neutral on Chinese equities overall and Attractive on A-shares. It forecasts 2027 earnings growth of 10.8% for MSCI China and 12% for the CSI 300.
IT is about 30% of the CSI 300 versus 11% of MSCI China, and industrial exposure is also larger onshore. This composition drives the A-share preference.

Within technology UBS prefers semiconductor equipment and selected hardware. It is more selective on offshore internet platforms because AI infrastructure spending could weigh on near-term free cash flow and shareholder returns.
UBS favors a barbell for 2027: selected technology, innovative health care and globally competitive Chinese companies, paired with quality dividends from large Chinese banks.
3Q26 GDP grew 4.5% y/y versus 4.3% in 2Q26, bringing January-September growth to 4.6% y/y. 3Q exports rose 28.4% y/y, retail sales grew 0.7% and fixed-asset investment contracted 10.0%.
UBS says the 3Q GDP rebound keeps the 4.5-5% full-year target within reach and reduces the likelihood of additional stimulus by year-end.
The EU is reportedly considering quotas or tariffs on Chinese chemicals, furniture and machinery imports, potentially from 1Q27, following restrictions on Chinese hybrid vehicles.

MSCI China fell 10.8% over the past month on macro risks and policy uncertainty. Export VAT rebate cuts for auto and battery companies raised profitability concerns. UBS believes much of the earnings risk is already priced in select sectors.

Chinese internet companies begin reporting 3Q earnings from mid-November, with valuations near multi-year lows, subdued positioning, high-teens 2027 earnings growth expectations and emerging positive revisions. No obvious near-term catalyst exists.
Chinese IG bonds gained 0.7% month to date (+0.3% YTD, 5.6% yield to maturity). High yield fell 1.0% (+3.3% YTD, 11.9% YTM) on spread widening in select property and industrial names.

UBS sees opportunities to selectively add high-quality Asia bonds at current yields and would avoid ultra-long duration. It favors a barbell of defensive China and Hong Kong IG with subordinated bank and insurance capital and short-dated Macau gaming bonds.

The Macau government launched a MOP 20bn Government Guidance Fund, with the six gaming operators contributing MOP 9bn in aggregate, which could add liquidity pressure for select operators. September GGR fell 1.2% y/y, the fourth straight monthly decline.
The late-September mortgage subsidy has stringent eligibility criteria and is expected to give only marginal housing support. September primary-market sales and prices kept falling.

USDCNY is near 6.67. UBS attributes CNY strength mainly to strong external flows and exporter FX conversions, not USD dynamics, and sees no sign the PBoC is less tolerant of gradual appreciation. Forecasts are 6.60 by year-end and 6.50 by mid-2027.

Tech stocks fell a single-digit percentage over the past month after a strong September. Meta fell after an earnings beat when it announced plans to issue a new class of shares, which spread AI-spending worries to Asian tech.

UBS keeps the structural AI thesis intact. It expects average cloud revenue growth to accelerate from 48% y/y in the June quarter to 58% in the September quarter, and cites rising GPU rental prices. It favors a barbell of AI semiconductor and hardware names plus mega-cap platforms and defensive tech.

sector_views.rationale: Macro risks and policy uncertainty warrant selectivity despite improved entry points.
Greater exposure to AI infrastructure, technology localization and advanced manufacturing, with upward 2027 IT earnings revisions.
AI infrastructure spending may weigh on near-term free cash flow and shareholder returns before monetization.
Pharma gains from commercialization, out-licensing and international expansion, and CDMOs have resilient outsourcing demand.
Improving net interest margins, earnings growth and higher payout ratios support dividends.
Barbell of high-quality semiconductor and hardware names tied to AI infrastructure spending, plus mega-cap platforms and defensive tech.
Limited stimulus, falling primary-market sales and prices. UBS credit favors developers with larger investment property portfolios and stronger balance sheets.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts 2027 earnings growth of 10.8% for MSCI China and 12% for the CSI 300 (forecast, not reported).
Chinese internet companies report 3Q26 earnings from mid-November (upcoming). 2027 earnings growth expectations are in the high teens (consensus/expectation) with emerging positive revisions.
Meta shares fell after its 3Q earnings beat when it announced a new class of shares to raise capital (reported, no EPS figures given).
UBS expects average cloud revenue growth to accelerate from 48% y/y in the June quarter to 58% y/y in the September quarter (forecast for the September quarter).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Full-year 2026 estimate within the official 4.5-5% target, with January-September growth already at 4.6% y/y.
Slower but stable growth with export momentum moderating and investment helping.
Up from 4.3% in 2Q26, keeping the full-year target within reach.
Export strength is offsetting weak domestic demand.
Slowdown as AI capex growth moderates and the comparison base rises.
UBS forecast, supported by external flows and a softer USD.
Down 32bps from its peak after a flight-to-quality bull-flattening of the curve.

trade_ideas.description: Selectively add high-quality Asia bonds, avoid ultra-long duration, in a barbell of defensive China and Hong Kong IG with subordinated bank and insurance capital and short-dated Macau gaming bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Current yield levels are compelling and Asia credit offers steady income with defensive characteristics.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher volatility in ultra-long duration bonds.

trade_ideas.description: Barbell in Chinese equities: semiconductor equipment and selected hardware, innovative pharma and CDMOs, globally competitive exporters, paired with large Chinese banks for dividends
trade_ideas.rationale: Balances growth, income and resilience as headline GDP stays stable.
trade_ideas.risk: Export VAT rebate cuts and trade barriers could trigger earnings revisions for exporters.

trade_ideas.description: Barbell within technology: high-quality semiconductor and hardware companies benefiting from AI infrastructure spending, plus mega-cap platforms and defensive tech
trade_ideas.rationale: Structural AI thesis remains intact, while concerns over AI capex financing call for selectivity.
trade_ideas.risk: Sustainability of AI infrastructure spending and its debt or equity financing.

risk_factors: Export VAT rebate cuts for auto and battery companies could trigger earnings revisions for export-oriented industrials.
The EU may impose quotas or tariffs on Chinese chemicals, furniture and machinery from 1Q27.
Property remains a drag, and the mortgage subsidy is expected to have only marginal impact.
Household deleveraging and fading trade-in subsidies constrain consumption.
AI capex moderation could slow exports, and concerns over AI infrastructure financing could pressure tech valuations.
Elevated global bond yields limit room for policy-rate cuts.
Macau operators face liquidity pressure from the Government Guidance Fund contributions amid weak gaming revenue.
Offshore internet platforms face near-term free cash flow pressure from AI infrastructure investment.
vol_and_positioning: Chinese internet positioning is described as subdued, with valuations near multi-year lows ahead of 3Q earnings from mid-November.
Chinese high yield spreads widened month to date on select property and industrial names.
geopolitical: Recent US-China leadership engagement has reduced the risk of near-term escalation.
Discussions with Europe on a hybrid vehicle quota arrangement have lowered some tail risks.
The EU is reportedly considering quotas or tariffs on Chinese chemicals, furniture and machinery from 1Q27.
Unresolved structural tensions mean tariffs and technology restrictions remain sources of uncertainty.
China's widening trade imbalance with the rest of the world could bring more trade barriers.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS says AI capital spending stays robust on healthy demand and better monetization, citing rising GPU rental prices, strong semiconductor results and cloud revenue growth accelerating from 48% to 58% y/y.
tension_points.bear_case: Concerns over the scale and financing of AI infrastructure spending triggered a big tech selloff, with Meta falling after announcing a new class of shares despite an earnings beat.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A moderation of the AI capex cycle, which UBS says would favor mega-cap platforms and defensive tech names over direct AI infrastructure beneficiaries.

tension_points.bull_case: Valuations are near multi-year lows, positioning is subdued, 2027 earnings growth expectations are in the high teens and positive revisions are emerging.
tension_points.bear_case: Macro risks, policy uncertainty and export VAT rebate cuts could trigger earnings revisions for export-oriented industrials, and no obvious near-term catalyst exists.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Export VAT rebate cuts broadening beyond autos and batteries, which UBS says is feared by the market.
